pr_title: drivers: clock_control: nrf: Use onoff service
pr_body:
Ported nRF clock control driver to use onoff service.
Clock_control API no longer tracks number of users but only enables or disables clock. It should not be used directly for clocks which have multiple user.

Clock control driver implements onoff service which can be used to track clock users. Clock control driver implements error detection mechanism which detects cases when direct API and onoff API is used for the same clock subsystem.

Nordic specific API (`nrf_clock_control.h`) provides function for getting onoff manager associated with given clock subsystem: `z_nrf_clock_control_get_onoff()`.

Since low frequency clock is typically used in enable once mode, nordic specific API provides a function for enabling LF clock without a need to maintain onoff client (`z_nrf_clock_control_lf_on()`). This is currently used by components which uses LF clock: system timer, bluetooth or counter driver.

PR contains port to use onoff service whenever HF clock is used.

PR is based on #23898 thus DNM.

Fixes #20712
pr_comments:
**All checks are passing now.**



*Tip: The bot edits this comment instead of posting a new one, so you can check the comment's history to see earlier messages.*

@pabigot
 
> The existing clock_control API doesn't work for Nordic;

The existing clock_control API was used differently by nordic and others. That is because majority of clocks have single user and does not need reference counting, etc. Nordic was using it differently, with clock control. We also added `struct clock_control_async_data` to asynchronous API to allow queueing requests.

With onoff ready, my idea is to simplify clock control API to be single user only. Clocks that may have multiple users must not use clock control API directly but rather access it using associated onoff service which is then the single user of the driver. I prefer that over expanding clock control API.

Also note that for nrf53 there are clocks which has only single user (e.g. dedicated 48Mhz USB clock) so even not all clock subsystems in nordic will have onoff service.

>There's some effort to make some standard clock_control API work using the new Nordic-specific API

API can be extended with that error codes.

The reality is that clock control API is used by vendor specific code since clock subsystem are vendor specific so standardize API does not provide portability but rather standardize pattern. Also decision whether use API directly or onoff requires specific knowledge.

issue_context.title: nRF clock_control_on() is nonblocking
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

Per discussion in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/20708, the non-async clock enable function `clock_control_on()` should block until the clock is ready, but the nRF clock driver doesn't.

**To Reproduce**

- call clock_control_on() on an nRF clock that isn't already enabled
- observe clock_start() in nrf_power_clock.c calls clock_async_start() directly with no callback
- without a callback, note clock_async_start() returns before the clock may be ready

**Expected behavior**

Clock status should be definitely ready by the time clock_control_on() returns.

**Impact**

Unknown.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 
nRF platform, possibly others.

**Additional context**

Discussion in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/20708 and https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/20710.
comments:
I was about to open an issue when I've found this one.

The nRF radio driver is hit by the nonblocking behavior of `clock_control_on` - the radio may malfunction when used before HF clock is ready, yet the radio driver itself does not take any extra action to verify that the clock is running as `clock_control_on` is supposed to block until clock is ready (and it used to work like this until  [this commit](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/6700f2f1940c645c5cd1eb23baad8bd0c8041b81)).
im working right now on clock_control driver to straighten this up (and start using onoff service)

review_comments: @tbursztyka @mnkp @jdascenzio @jfischer-phytec-iot @galak @mbolivar-nordic feedback welcome on this new pattern: obtaining an instance to the on/off service through the existing driver API.

I did not see any changes on the public API side. Instead, it exposes private features to this driver. I don't have much opinion on this then. If that's solving an important nordic use case but has no grounds for being generalized, the there is no other way. Fine by me.
I agree. At dev-review there was no feedback that others had similar requirements, so it seems appropriate to do it this way, at least to get started.

Yes.  The original design concept did not expect these structures to be exposed, but in this case it's the most sensible approach.  The expected alternative (provide custom request/release API specific to the subsystem) can be demonstrated where there's value added by the wrappers.
#22409 had the proposal to make it more generic but since there are no other vendors with such requirement we can keep it private.
`atomic_dec` returns previous value. So 1 means that refcnt reached 0.
This will wait only when `MULTITHREADING` is enabled in Kconfig.

`clock_control_on` in 'clock_control.h' states
```
This function may sleep, and thus can only be called from thread context.
```
For me it means that it can only be called from app which supports multithreading.
We could extend description to state that in non sleepable context it just spins and then extend implementation.

I think that "from thread context" in that description is supposed to mean "not from ISR". And someone may want to call this function from `main()` in an app without `MULTITHREADING` enabled. An attempt to call `k_sem_take` with a parameter other than `K_NO_WAIT` will end up in UsageFault then (I thought it would just not wait but apparently I was wrong). I think this case should be handled somehow, perhaps with a loop calling `k_cpu_idle()` while waiting for this semaphore.
just learn that interrupts does not work if multhreading is off (#26796). I will return error in that case.
This propagates to a behavior change to `led_strip_update_rgb()`: `clock_control_off` returns zero on success; `onoff_release()` may return a positive value on success.

`lll_clock_wait` is blocking LFCLOCK request. Here, now, only semaphores are taken and given?
fixed.
semaphore is not needed for non-blocking calls.
`lll_clock_init` is non-blocking LFCLOCK request interface. Semaphores should not be given.
